To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) finite element energy minimizing sequences exist and are bounded in a suitable energy norm; (2) finite element energy minimizing sequences converge to a finite energy minimizer; and (3) the finite element energy minimizing sequence converges to a minimizer of the energy in the sense that it converges in the energy norm.

(1) the minimum energy over the class of admissible finite element functions is bounded below by the minimum energy over a finite element subspace; (2) a finite element energy-minimizers sequence can be used to obtain a lower bound on the minimum energy; and (3) the energy of the finite element energy-minimizer converges to the minimum energy over admissible functions.

(1) the finite element method can be used to approximate the minimum energy over admissible finite element spaces; and (2) the error in the energy between the finite element approximation and the minimum energy can be controlled by a parameter that is related to the number of degrees of freedom in the finite element model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical analysis of the multi-well problem.
the numerical approximation of a class and the analysis of the finite element method for the class of microstructures.
the mathematical analysis of the finite element approximation to a class of stress- free martensitic microstructure modeled by the multi-well energy functional.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy of a finite element minimizer is within a constant multiple of the energy of a continuous energy minimizer.
the finite element method is an effective numerical tool in the study of multi-well energy functionals.
, for any given admissible finite element deformation, the error in the finite element energy-minimizers can be made as small as desired by choosing a fine enough finite element triangulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite element approximation converges to a solution of the multi-well minimization problem.
, in the context of finite element energy minimization, we can obtain bounds for the minimum energy and the error estimates for the energy-minimizing sequence.
we have shown that, in the context of the finite element method, the multi-well energy model for stress-free martensites has a well-defined limit, which is the same as the one obtained in [1].
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in a certain regime, the error between the finite element energy minimizer and the exact energy minimizer is bounded by a constant times the square of the error between the corresponding finite element minimizer and a finite element solution to the associated linearized system.
, for a fixed mesh size h and for sufficiently small loads, the finite element energy minimizer is a good approximation to the energy minimizer.
the error in the energy of finite element energy minimization converges to zero as the mesh is refined.
